# JS-modules
> Small, dependency-free JavaScript modules and tools for single-file browser games and apps, extracted from Apple Press and Fancy, the Banana. MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 LFC Foundry.

Each module is one file usable as a browser global or via require(). Start with modules.json (machine-readable index).

Grouped by what each piece does: Modules & Tools (43, tools included), Story editor packages (10) and AI knowledge base (1). Every entry in modules.json carries a `category`.

## Modules & Tools: Device and browser adaptation
- [env-probes](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/env-probes/README.md): Detects privacy modes that round timers (including Firefox's 16.67 ms clock), scramble canvas read-back or block storage, and says what it found in plain words. (global EnvProbes) Version 1.1.0, API 1.
- [frame-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/frame-kit/README.md): Frame pacing for canvas games: even-dt smooths the frame time, quality-governor steps effects down and back up, job-pump spreads heavy jobs across frames, frame-meter shows frames a second, hitches and tap delay in plain words. (global EvenDt, QualityGovernor, JobPump, FrameMeter) Version 1.2.1, API 1.
- [field-report](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/field-report/README.md): Two hidden buttons for a game or app: five taps in a corner open a panel that saves a speed report (start-up, frames a second, slowest frames, heavy tasks, plain verdict) and an error log, as small Markdown files. No network. (global FieldReport) Version 1.0.2, API 1.
- [fx-governor](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/fx-governor/README.md): Steps visual effects down when the device cannot keep up; never back up behind the player. (global FxGovernor) Version 1.1.1, API 1.
- [gpu-blur](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/gpu-blur/README.md): Blurs a picture (a canvas, an ImageBitmap or RGBA bytes) on the graphics card with WebGL 2, or in WebAssembly, or in plain JavaScript, whichever the device does best; every way gives the same picture, and a big blur never freezes the page. (global GpuBlur) Version 1.3.0, API 1.
- [image-decode](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/image-decode/README.md): Loads PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF pictures so the page does not freeze when they are first drawn: picks the right off-thread way for each browser, loads a list in order, and tells whether the browser can read WebP or AVIF. (global ImageDecode) Version 1.2.2, API 1.
- [slow-note](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/slow-note/README.md): Keeps a short note, only on the device, of the errors, slow taps and long frames a page had; copyable as plain text, nothing is sent anywhere. Version 1.0.0, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Saving and data safety
- [save-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/save-kit/README.md): Safe localStorage saves, backup slot, checksummed copy-paste save codes with a size limit on what a paste may unpack to. (global SaveKit) Version 1.3.1, API 1.
- [tab-guard](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/tab-guard/README.md): Keeps one open copy of a page in charge (Web Locks), so two tabs do not overwrite each other's saved data, and tells the game when the other copy closes. (global TabGuard) Version 1.1.1, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Games - Looks and effects
- [cartoon-3d-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/cartoon-3d-kit/README.md): A written style guide plus demo for the soft, glossy cartoon 3D look done in plain CSS and SVG. Version 1.3.0, API 1.
- [fly-to-mini](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/fly-to-mini/README.md): A big element scrolls away and a copy flies to its sticky mini version (and back). (global FlyToMini) Version 1.2.0, API 1.
- [sprite-baker](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/sprite-baker/README.md): Tiny software 3D rasterizer that bakes shaded sprites to canvases once at load, or one frame per tick; also makes silhouette masks and packs sprite sheets. Optional WebAssembly fill add-on (same pixels, about 1.1 to 1.4 times faster baking in Chromium and Firefox). (global SpriteBaker) Version 1.7.1, API 1.
- [stage-curtains](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/stage-curtains/README.md): Velvet stage curtains that slide shut over a page, then fly open; the velvet is painted by a small WebAssembly loop with plain JavaScript as the fallback. (global StageCurtains) Version 1.4.1, API 1.
- [sticker-text](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/sticker-text/README.md): Die-cut sticker lettering in plain CSS text-shadow rings, no images. (global StickerText) Version 1.1.0, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Games - Controls
- [back-close](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/back-close/README.md): Makes the phone back swipe or back button close the top panel instead of leaving the page (CloseWatcher, with an opt-in history fallback for browsers without it). (global BackClose) Version 1.2.0, API 1.
- [hold-press](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/hold-press/README.md): Hold-to-repeat for buttons that survives Android Chrome pointercancel. (global HoldPress) Version 1.1.0, API 1.
- [pad-nav](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/pad-nav/README.md): Gamepad API to DOM focus: move through buttons, menus, sliders and drop-downs with a controller, no game code. (global PadNav) Version 1.1.0, API 1.
- [wake-keeper](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/wake-keeper/README.md): Keeps the screen awake only while a game wants it: released on pause, hidden tab and idle, asked again when allowed, no retry storms. (global WakeKeeper) Version 1.1.0, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Games - Assist
- [grown-ups-door](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/grown-ups-door/README.md): A hold-then-drag task a young child will not finish, in front of the buttons and links a grown-up should press (a speed bump, not security). Version 1.0.0, API 1.
- [spotlight-tour](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/spotlight-tour/README.md): A first-time tour: one dimmed layer, a bright window over the current part, Skip and Back, remembers who saw it and gives a finishing gift once. Version 1.1.1, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Games - Math
- [idle-core](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/idle-core/README.md): Tested maths for idle/clicker games: costs, buy-many and buy-max, milestones, away income, boost queue, number format. (global IdleCore) Version 1.2.0, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Games - Testing
- [canvas-probe](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/canvas-probe/README.md): Test-build counter for canvas 2D games: calls per frame, save/restore leaks, overhanging drawImage sources, draws below half size, style-write repeats, painted area. Version 1.1.1, API 1.
- [firefox-stand-in](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/firefox-stand-in/README.md): Runs a Playwright-for-Python test in stock Firefox (through Selenium and geckodriver) without rewriting it; says plainly which calls it supports and stops with a clear message on the rest. Version 1.1.0, API 1.
- [fuzz-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/fuzz-kit/README.md): Seeded, reproducible random-input fuzzer engine with weighted operations, invariants, liveness checks and failure shrinking; Playwright and Puppeteer runners with real input and CPU throttling; stock-Firefox recipe; test-hook stripper. Version 1.3.4, API 1.
- [speed-guard](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/speed-guard/README.md): One command that says whether a release got slower than the one before it, from the speed-history files, and which browser checks a change needs re-run. It runs nothing itself, so it costs no browser time. Version 1.0.0, API 1.
- [speed-lab](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/speed-lab/README.md): One-button speed test run on the device: compares your page with parts switched off, keeps the scene in view and uncovered, and says the answer in plain sentences with a copyable table. Version 1.1.1, API 1.
- [storage-probe](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/storage-probe/README.md): Page that tells you in plain words whether copies of a page saved in different folders share their saved data, see each other's writes and locks; one button, copyable report. Version 1.1.0, API 1.
- [test-isolation](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/test-isolation/README.md): Puts a prefix in front of every localStorage key on a test page, so a speed test or random-play run never touches the real saved game. Version 1.1.0, API 1.
- [test-runner](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/test-runner/README.md): Shared pieces for browser checks and speed tests: warm browsers, a four-browser runner, fair timing, skip-unchanged wasm builds, a wasm-versus-JavaScript twin test, a picture fingerprint gate and an automatic bisect. Version 1.3.0, API 1.
- [webkit-driver](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/webkit-driver/README.md): Drives WebKitGTK or GNOME Web from Node with no dependencies, using the call names of Playwright and Puppeteer (goto, evaluate, waitForFunction, mouse, keyboard, screenshot, console errors), so a test written for them can also run in WebKit. Version 1.4.1, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: App - Efficiency
- [elias-fano](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/elias-fano/README.md): Keeps sorted whole numbers (ids, positions, links of every item of a map) in a third to a half of the memory of plain arrays and still answers 'value number i' and 'first value at or above x' without unpacking; also keeps many sorted lists in one structure and decodes them all at once. WebAssembly with SIMD, plain JavaScript fallback with the same answers. Version 1.5.0, API 1.
- [graph-walk](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/graph-walk/README.md): The two walks map and flow tools keep rewriting: breadth-first distances from an item, and a depth-first pass that marks the links that close a loop and lists items in finishing order. Typed arrays, no recursion, no dependencies. Version 0.7.2, API 0.
- [lfc-pack](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/lfc-pack/README.md): Packs newline-delimited JSON (logs, events, API dumps) into LFC-pack (.json.lfc): every field becomes a typed column inside zstd blocks, with a footer of per-block number ranges. Reads back the same rows as JSON.parse (or the exact original bytes), only some keys, or only a time range, with helper workers for big files. WebAssembly is required; a Python reader is included. Version 0.3.1, API 0.
- [text-columns](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/text-columns/README.md): Reads CSV or TSV text into typed columns: plain decimal columns become Float64Array parsed from the bytes, the rest stay text; the field scan runs in WebAssembly SIMD with a plain JavaScript fallback giving the same answers. Quoted fields, CRLF and byte-order marks work; ragged rows throw. Version 0.6.2, API 0.
- [memory-compression](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/memory-compression/README.md): Keeps big data packed in memory and brings it back exactly, in one file with one pack/unpack: bytes and typed arrays (a 120 MB scene shrinks to 52%, 41% in small mode, and restores in about 239 ms in Firefox 158.0, against 312 ms with lz4-wasm and 1.5 s with fflate; lower is better) and big lists of plain JavaScript objects (300,000 link objects shrink to 14% of their JSON text, 35% for msgpackr with records). Picks the right layer by itself; MemoryCompressionJSO stays as an alias. Version 2.7.0, API 2.
- [single-file-tools](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/single-file-tools/README.md): Font subsetting, safe inline-SVG tightening and a Zopfli self-extracting packer for one-file games. Version 1.2.0, API 1.

## Modules & Tools: Model simulation
- [walker-sim](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/walker-sim/README.md): Simulates random walkers on a network with seeded, repeatable runs, 16 random-number distributions, 95% ranges and the exact odds to check against (1,000,000 walkers in about 52 ms with the WebAssembly loop in Chromium 155 and Firefox 158, lower is better). Big runs use a WebAssembly loop first, JavaScript when it cannot. Version 2.4.0, API 2.

## Modules & Tools: Visualization
- [gif-writer](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/gif-writer/README.md): Writes animated GIFs from canvas pictures with one shared palette, storing only the pixels that changed (about 6.8 times smaller than gifenc on a mostly still animation). Version 1.6.1, API 1.
- [clip-writer](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/clip-writer/README.md): Turns pictures into a short MP4 or WebM video in the browser with the browser's own video encoder and two small file writers, no libraries; the same add/finish shape as gif-writer, and about 8 times smaller than a GIF of the same pictures in Netflow Map. Version 1.3.0, API 1.
- [netflow-engine](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/netflow-engine/README.md): The engine of Netflow Map as a module you can copy and adapt: nine views of a map and eleven network layouts, no two items on top of each other, WebAssembly twins for Force and Distances, and a use() hand-over for the layers and Sankey add-ons; a 30,000-item network lays out in about 0.8 s in the Netflow Map app (Firefox). Version 2.2.2, API 2.
- [netflow-layers](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/netflow-layers/README.md): Lays out a graph in rows (top to bottom or left to right) with story order, tags instead of very long links, a column for the pages every route passes, and tall maps cut into columns. Version 1.5.1, API 1.
- [netflow-scene](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/netflow-scene/README.md): Turns a Netflow Map layout into plain drawing lists that Canvas 2D, WebGL2, WebGPU or SVG can draw the same way; big flat maps keep links in typed lists and reuse link looks between pictures. Version 1.3.1, API 1.
- [netflow-sankey](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/netflow-sankey/README.md): Lays out a flow chart (Sankey) from a plain list of links, with about half the weighted crossings of d3-sankey on the charts measured, backward links drawn instead of crashing, and an SVG drawer. Version 2.3.2, API 2.

## Modules & Tools: Size and packaging
- [lzma-decode](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/lzma-decode/README.md): LZMA1 decoder that uses WebAssembly first (about 1.5 to 2.6 times faster to open a page) and falls back to a small readable ES5 JavaScript decoder; tested against Python's lzma. Browsers can only unpack gzip and deflate natively. (global lzmaDecode) Version 1.3.0, API 1.
- [lzma-pack](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/lzma-pack/README.md): Packs one HTML file into a smaller self-unpacking file with LZMA and a hash check (Python 3 standard library). Version 2.0.0, API 2.
- [pcodec-js](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/pcodec-js/README.md): Pcodec for web pages: unpacks (and optionally packs) big lists of numbers in a browser, one file, same bytes as any other Pcodec. The unpack-only file is 61 KB gzipped (the other JavaScript build of Pcodec is 324 KB), streams a 4,000,000-number file in 6.3 MB of memory, and WebAssembly is required (no plain-JavaScript backup). Version 1.6.1, API 1.
- [ppmd-decode](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/ppmd-decode/README.md): A PPMd (7-Zip PPMd7) decoder that uses WebAssembly first (about 1.4 to 1.8 times faster to open a page) and falls back to one ES5 JavaScript function, about 6.6 KB packed. It unpacks web-page data about 10% smaller than LZMA, but slower. PPMd is by Dmitry Shkarin; the public-domain code it follows is Igor Pavlov's, from 7-Zip. (global ppmd7Decode) Version 1.3.0, API 1.
- [ppmd-pack](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/tools/ppmd-pack/README.md): Packs one HTML file into a self-unpacking file with PPMd, the 7-Zip text compressor (PPMd by Dmitry Shkarin; public-domain code by Igor Pavlov, 7-Zip). Pure Python; pays off above about 60 KB of compressed data. Version 2.0.0, API 2.
- [zip-open](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules/zip-open/README.md): Opens .zip and Excel .xlsx files safely: limits counted on what really unpacks, so a zip bomb stops at the limit with a plain-words note. Version 1.5.1, API 1.

## Story editor packages: Story data (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [story-diff](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/story-diff/README.md): Says in plain words what one edit did to a story, such as "Add page “The Cellar”".
- [story-format](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/story-format/README.md): Create, clean, search, import and export interactive stories as JSON, with a JSON Schema. Twine import lives in twine-import.
- [story-outline](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/story-outline/README.md): Turns an indented outline into pages and choices, or into a whole branching story.
- [twine-import](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/twine-import/README.md): Reads Twine stories (Twine 2 HTML, Twee 3, Twine 1) and turns SugarCube and Harlowe code into rules, with a plain-words report.

## Story editor packages: Story validation (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [story-check](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/story-check/README.md): Exact checker for branching stories with items, numbers and dice: dead ends and endings no player can reach.

## Story editor packages: Story flow (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [story-map](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/story-map/README.md): Layered, arc and matrix drawings of a story graph (SVG) and seeded simulated players.

## Story editor packages: Story build and distribute (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [story-player](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/story-player/README.md): Build one offline HTML game from a story, or play a story from code or a terminal.

## Story editor packages: Story packaging (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [zip-page](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/zip-page/README.md): Wrap a finished HTML page into a smaller page that unzips itself, with a pure-JS inflater fallback.

## Story editor packages: Story testing (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [contract-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/contract-kit/README.md): A guide and a helper (about 7.2 KB minified) for keeping two implementations of one rule set from drifting apart: seeded random inputs, a side-by-side comparison (also for async functions), shrinking a failing input to a small one, a field table and a time limit; runs in browsers too.
- [qa-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/qa-kit/README.md): Tiered test runner and a Playwright-style API over WebDriver BiDi for stock Firefox; seeded random-story generator.

## AI knowledge base: Working with an AI helper (in https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor, generated from the Story Editor's sources)
- [ai-collab-kit](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/story-editor/blob/main/packages/ai-collab-kit/README.md): A written process and templates for a person and an AI assistant building software together.

## Docs
- [README](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/README.md): overview and install
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for AI assistants editing this repo
- [modules.json](https://github.com/lfcfoundry/JS-modules/blob/main/modules.json): index with files, globals and demo paths
- Test browsers: only those on the `browsers` branch of the private knowledge-base repository: Firefox 158, ungoogled Chromium 155 and WebKitGTK 2.52.6 (Linux), one at a time; re-read that branch's README before each run and label results with the exact version. Chromium 141 and 153 and Firefox 157 are retired. Every module's README and changelog entry has a "Tested in" line naming the browsers used. Real phones and Safari itself are not checked yet. See the Tests section of the README and AGENTS.md.
